comparisons.peer_summary: Liquidity is defined as cash and high-quality, liquid, unencumbered securities used to meet obligations; the company manages this position through line-of-business, ALM, and legal entity funding strategies on both forward and current bases.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC define liquidity through the lens of highly liquid, unencumbered assets and affirm the appropriateness of their positions using internal models and qualitative assessments. BAC specifically defines liquidity as 'cash and high-quality, liquid, unencumbered securities' used to meet obligations and manages this via centralized strategies. GS similarly states its liquidity position was 'appropriate' based on 'internal liquidity risk models' and 'qualitative assessment'. While GS focuses on the outcome (appropriateness of position) and BAC focuses on the definition and management structure, both address the core assessment of sufficient liquid resources.

sentences.text: Based on the results of our internal liquidity risk models, described above, as well as our consideration of other factors, including, but not limited to, a qualitative assessment of our condition, as well as the financial markets, we believe our liquidity position as of both December 2024 and December 2023 was appropriate.

We define liquidity as readily available assets, limited to cash and high-quality, liquid, unencumbered securities that we can use to meet our contractual and contingent financial obligations as they arise.

We believe that a centralized approach to funding and liquidity management enhances our ability to monitor liquidity requirements, maximizes access to funding sources, minimizes borrowing costs and facilitates timely responses to liquidity events.

comparisons.peer_topic: Liquidity risk factors and management objectives
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi manages liquidity risk arising from external factors like market disruptions and credit spreads, aiming to fund its asset base, grow core businesses, maintain sufficient liquidity for adverse circumstances, and satisfy regulatory requirements including resolution planning.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi frame their liquidity assessment around maintaining sufficient liquidity to operate under adverse circumstances and satisfy regulatory requirements. Citi explicitly states its management objectives include 'maintaining sufficient liquidity... so that Citi can operate under a variety of adverse circumstances' and 'satisfying regulatory requirements'. GS affirms its liquidity position was 'appropriate' based on internal models and qualitative assessments of its condition and financial markets, implying a similar goal of operational resilience and compliance with market/regulatory expectations. Both disclosures focus on the strategic adequacy of liquidity rather than just definitional mechanics.

sentences.text: Based on the results of our internal liquidity risk models, described above, as well as our consideration of other factors, including, but not limited to, a qualitative assessment of our condition, as well as the financial markets, we believe our liquidity position as of both December 2024 and December 2023 was appropriate.

Citi's funding and liquidity management objectives are aimed at (i) funding its existing asset base, (ii) growing its core businesses, (iii) maintaining sufficient liquidity, structured appropriately, so that Citi can operate under a variety of adverse circumstances, including potential Company-specific and/or market liquidity events in varying durations and severity, and (iv) satisfying regulatory requirements, including, but not limited to, those related to resolution planning (see "Resolution Plan" and "Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC)" below).

comparisons.peer_summary: Liquidity risk is defined as the risk that the Firm will be unable to meet its cash and collateral needs as they arise or lacks the appropriate amount, composition, and tenor of funding and liquidity to support its assets and liabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the fundamental nature of liquidity risk and the need for adequate funding. JPM defines liquidity risk as the inability to meet cash/collateral needs or lacking the 'appropriate amount, composition and tenor of funding'. GS assesses its 'liquidity position' as 'appropriate' using internal models. While JPM provides a risk definition and GS provides a position assessment, they share the underlying theme of ensuring the firm has the right type and amount of funding/liquidity to support its business. GS's assertion of an 'appropriate' position is the operational realization of the risk definition provided by JPM.

sentences.text: Based on the results of our internal liquidity risk models, described above, as well as our consideration of other factors, including, but not limited to, a qualitative assessment of our condition, as well as the financial markets, we believe our liquidity position as of both December 2024 and December 2023 was appropriate.

Liquidity risk is the risk that the Firm will be unable to meet its cash and collateral needs as they arise or that it does not have the appropriate amount, composition and tenor of funding and liquidity to support its assets and liabilities.

comparisons.peer_summary: The core components supporting the company's target liquidity profile are the Required Liquidity Framework, Liquidity Stress Tests, and Liquidity Resources.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley describe the framework or components used to ensure and support their liquidity position. MS identifies its 'Required Liquidity Framework, Liquidity Stress Tests and Liquidity Resources' as the core components supporting its target liquidity profile. GS similarly relies on 'internal liquidity risk models' (which function as stress tests/frameworks) and qualitative assessments to determine that its liquidity position is 'appropriate'. Both disclose the structural approach to validating their liquidity adequacy.

sentences.text: Based on the results of our internal liquidity risk models, described above, as well as our consideration of other factors, including, but not limited to, a qualitative assessment of our condition, as well as the financial markets, we believe our liquidity position as of both December 2024 and December 2023 was appropriate.
